implementation_notes: C# absorbed CPS into async/await: an async method is a state machine whose continuations are generated by the compiler, and await is the syntactic form of applying the continuation. Task.ContinueWith is the explicit, un-sugared continuation - a delegate that receives the antecedent task, which is literally a CPS function. For hand-written continuations, use Func<T, TResult> and compose with ContinueWith, being careful that ContinueWith on a faulted task runs on the fault path rather than skipping it, and that TaskScheduler.Unobserved can surface an exception nobody awaited.
idiom_name: async/await (compiler-generated CPS); Task.ContinueWith for the explicit continuation
pitfalls: ContinueWith without OnlyOnRanToCompletion runs on the fault and cancellation paths too, so the success body must re-throw or guard.
Task.Run wraps work in a thread-pool thread and defeats the purpose when the code is already asynchronous.
Blocking on .Result or .Wait() inside an async method deadlocks in a single-threaded synchronization context such as a UI or ASP.NET classic handler.
